summary: The transfer correction was accepted, and its consequence was that the account still claimed an election cost with no receipt isolating it, since the source finding showed the entry-point receipts also enqueue an automatic transfer to a voter. This turn builds that receipt: one explicit LeadershipTransferToServer per case, the automatic form never called, on a fresh four-member cluster whose named target is either a demoted non-voter or an ordinary voter, with leader state and every member's term sampled every 10 ms for five seconds. I dry-ran the exact file in the local tree before submitting it. The trigger recorded the future returning nil in 0 ms with the named member never leading, seven leaderless samples over 471, and the maximum term rising from two to four, while the control installed its named voter with a single leaderless sample and a single term advance. That contrast is what lets the account attribute disruption to the explicit request rather than to a neighbouring call. The request declares the two case prerequisites on each target's own configuration view, asserts that an admitted transfer installs its named member in both cases and that the trigger pays no leaderless interval, and carries both transfer knowledge entries at revision 10. The harness compiles and passes under the focused test name, and the submission validates against the schema.
